title: Redline snippets + priority matrix (personal scratch)
content:
Purpose: quick personal scratchpad for contract calls / redline snippets I reuse. Not polished — mix of short scripts, prioritized clauses, fallback concessions, and sample language. Use when prepping negotiations with AE + Solutions engineer.

Top-level negotiating priorities (short):
- P0 (must protect / escalate): Liability cap, Indemnity carveouts for customer data, Data residency & export, Data use (training), Security obligations + KPIs, Subpoena handling.
- P1 (strong preference to land): Confidentiality narrowness, Termination for convenience notice / cure periods, Source code/derivative IP carveouts, Audit scope and frequency.
- P2 (nice-to-have / economic): Payment milestones, SLA credits calculation, Publicity/case studies, minor warranty clarifications.

Priority matrix (quick view):
- Liability Cap: P0. Target: $500k or 3x fees (whichever higher for small deals); Always tie to fees for commercial deals. If counterparty insists on unlimited for breach of confidentiality, offer narrow exception for willful misconduct only.
  - Sample redline: "Cap on aggregate liability shall not exceed the greater of (a) $500,000 or (b) three times the fees paid by Customer in the 12 months preceding the claim. For claims arising from gross negligence or willful misconduct, the foregoing cap shall not apply."

- Indemnity: P0. Push back on broad IP indemnity that requires Redwood to defend broadly when customer's misuse triggers claim. Limit Redwood obligation to third-party IP claims alleging direct infringement by unmodified models/services as delivered.
  - Sample redline: "Vendor shall indemnify Customer for third-party claims alleging that the Service, as provided by Vendor without modification, directly infringes a third party’s U.S. patents, copyrights, or trademarks. Vendor’s obligation does not cover claims arising from (i) Customer’s combination of the Service with other products, or (ii) Customer-provided prompts or data."

- Data use & training: P0. Redwood policy: we do not train customer-specific models on customer confidential data unless a signed addendum. Keep language explicit and reversible.
  - Defensive snippet: "Vendor will not use Customer Data to improve or train Vendor’s models, services, or models offered to third parties, except as expressly set forth in a written addendum. Vendor may use aggregated/ de-identified metrics for operational purposes provided such data cannot be re-associated with Customer."

- Data residency & export: P0 for regulated customers. If they require EU-only residency, require product team input (SRE + infra) to confirm feasibility and lead time.
  - Quick ask for SE call: Which regions can we pin? Are there special egress costs? Who owns support for cross-region fallback?

- Security obligations & audit: P0/P1. Accept SOC2 report + gap plan rather than open-ended right to audit. If customer insists on audit, limit to one annual audit, scoped to Redwood’s scope for the Service, and use standard audit providers.
  - Sample redline: "Customer may request evidence of Vendor’s compliance (SOC2 or equivalent). Vendor will provide reasonable evidence and respond to material security findings within 60 days. On-site audits are limited to (i) one time per 12 months, and (ii) scope to Vendor’s systems that directly process Customer Data."

- Confidentiality: P1. Keep term finite (3–5 years) and carve out aggregated telemetry permitted for product improvement under the Data use clause.

- Termination: P1. Favor 30–60 day cure periods for material breach. For termination for convenience, negotiate 90-day notice + pro rata refunds on committed capacity. For Dedicated customers, include wind-down SLAs for data deletion and transfer assistance.

- Subpoena / Law enforcement requests: P0. Need clear procedure and notice obligations to customer where permitted. Avoid wholesale broad rights to disclose.
  - Language: "Vendor will notify Customer of any legal request for Customer Data prior to disclosure to the extent permitted by law and will cooperate with reasonable lawful requests for assistance."

Negotiation scripts / lines to use (short)
- When they push a high cap: "We're an infra provider; unlimited liability for third-party business losses would require pricing + insurance we don't carry for self-serve. Let's identify a commercial cap tied to fees and limited exceptions for willful wrongdoing."
- When they ask to train on their data: "We can offer a dedicated-training addendum with specific controls and pricing. Default is no training on customer confidential data."
- On audit asks: "We can share SOC2 + penetration test summaries and remediate material findings; on-site audits require narrow scoping and mutual NDA."

Fallback concessions (if must move on):
- Increase notice/cure period before termination.
- Agree to one scoped, third-party audit per year with costs shared.
- Accept higher cap if customer pre-pays X months of committed capacity or agrees to annual commitment.

Quick redline snippets I re-use (copy/paste ready):
1) Liability cap template (short): "The aggregate liability of Vendor for all claims arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (a) $500,000 and (b) the fees paid by Customer to Vendor in the 12 months preceding the claim."
2) Training/data use: "Vendor shall not use Customer Data to improve or train Vendor’s models or services without Customer’s prior written consent."
3) Indemnity scope: "Vendor’s indemnity obligation is limited to direct claims by third parties alleging infringement caused by Vendor’s unmodified Service as delivered."
4) Audit cap: "On-site audits are limited to one per 12 months and to systems that directly process Customer Data."

Operational questions to resolve before call (RACI-style notes):
- Who owns confirming data deletion timelines for Private deployments? (tag: infra)
- How long to spin EU-only deployment? (tag: infra/product)
- Can we provide SOC2 artifacts for partner-level redactions? (tag: security)
- Will SE team accept pro rata refunds for committed capacity if we sell Dedicated? (tag: sales/finance)

Unresolved items / TODOs before sending initial redline:
- Confirm insurance thresholds available from Finance (need figure for higher cap offers).
- Get SRE confirmation on regional pinning feasibility and egress pricing.
- Draft addendum for "training on data" that includes controls, deleteability, and pricing.

Notes from prior calls (bite-sized):
- Customer A insisted on 3x fees cap — they accept $1M floor for platform; used that as template for mid-market deals.
- Enterprise deals often want direct audit; offering SOC2 + written remediation plan closed 2 deals last quarter.

Quick mental checklist for redline session:
- Start with P0s: cap, indemnity narrowness, data-use.
- Keep language specific and machine-actionable where possible (dates, limits, service names).
- Avoid ambiguous absolutes (like "all data" without definition).
- Have fallback concessions lined up and a price/commitment ask tied to each concession.

Personal negotiation script snippets (short & human):
- "We built this product to be used by businesses — our standard risk allocation is apolitical and tied to usage. If you need different allocation, let's discuss commercial balancing (commitments, insurance, or additional support)."
- "We can't train on customer confidential data without a signed addendum and controls — but we can offer a dedicated-training plan if that's a hard requirement."

End of scratchpad. Keep this as a living doc: add new snippets, outcomes from each negotiation, and pricing tradeoffs that worked.

Unresolved / later: collect 3 anonymized clause examples (with redlines) that closed last 6 enterprise deals and add here for patterns.
